detailed_description: Salary Calculator converts a single pay amount between hourly, daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, and annual views in the browser. Choose the input pay frequency, currency display, weekly hours, and an optional tax rate to compare before-tax and after-tax estimates side by side. The calculation uses 52 weeks, 5 workdays per week, and 12 months as simple assumptions. It is useful for quick job-offer comparisons, freelance planning, and household budgeting, but it is only a planning estimate and does not model extra compensation rules, benefits, local tax law, or rate conversion.
usage_steps: Enter the pay amount and choose whether it is hourly, daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, or annual.
Select the currency used for display. The selected currency does not convert exchange rates.
Adjust weekly hours if the default 40-hour week does not match your situation.
Set a tax-rate percentage if you want a rough after-tax estimate.
Compare the before-tax and after-tax results across all supported pay periods.
usage_examples: Convert a $95,000 annual offer into monthly, biweekly, weekly, daily, and hourly estimates.
Estimate the annual equivalent of a part-time hourly rate with fewer than 40 hours per week.
Compare two offers by putting both into the same monthly or annual view.
Use a rough tax percentage to plan take-home income before checking official payroll numbers.

faqs.question: Does this calculate official payroll taxes?
faqs.answer: No. The tax-rate field is a simple percentage estimate. Official payroll, benefits, and local tax rules should be checked separately.

faqs.question: Does the currency selector convert exchange rates?
faqs.answer: No. It only changes number formatting. Enter an amount that is already in the currency you want to compare.

faqs.question: What assumptions are used for conversions?
faqs.answer: The calculator uses 52 weeks per year, 5 workdays per week, and 12 months per year, with weekly hours controlled by your input.
